summary: Compare the best Clay alternatives for lead enrichment and prospecting. Honest breakdown of tools, workflows, and when each option fits SDR teams and founders.
body_markdown:
## What Are the Best Alternatives to Clay for Lead Enrichment and Prospecting?


**Orange Slice** , Apollo.io, Clearbit (now HubSpot Enrichment), Lusha, and Phantombuster are the main Clay alternatives worth evaluating in 2025. Each solves a different version of the problem.


Clay is a capable tool. It pulls from dozens of data providers, supports waterfall enrichment, and lets technical operators build sophisticated enrichment logic inside a spreadsheet. But it's not the right fit for every team — and the teams looking for a Clay alternative usually have a specific reason.


The most common ones: the credit costs grew faster than expected, the SDRs can't use it without RevOps help, or the team needs a prospecting database built in rather than bolted on. This article breaks down the honest alternatives, what each one does well, and where each one falls short.


---


## Why Do Teams Switch Away from Clay?


Before comparing tools, it's worth naming the actual friction points.


**Credit model complexity.** Clay charges credits per enrichment action, and the math gets complicated fast when you're running waterfall sequences across thousands of rows. Teams often hit their plan limit mid-campaign.


**Steep learning curve.** Clay is built for operators who think in spreadsheet formulas and API calls. SDRs who just want a list with verified emails often find it overwhelming.


**No native prospecting database.** Clay enriches records you bring to it. If you want to find net-new contacts matching an ICP, you need a separate tool feeding it — Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, or a scraper.


**CRM sync friction.** Exporting enriched data back to Salesforce or HubSpot cleanly requires mapping work that non-technical users often get wrong.


None of these are dealbreakers for the right team. But if any of them describe your situation, the alternatives below are worth a hard look.

## Tool-by-Tool Breakdown


### Is Orange Slice a Viable Clay Alternative?


[Orange Slice](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/data-enrichment-agent) is a chat-first smart spreadsheet that handles prospecting, enrichment, and qualification in one place. You describe your ICP in plain English — "Series A SaaS companies in the US with 20–100 employees hiring a VP of Sales" — and the columns populate automatically from LinkedIn intelligence, verified emails and phones, firmographics, funding data, tech stack, hiring signals, and a natural-language browser agent that can scrape any site.


The credit model only charges when data is actually found, which removes the anxiety of burning credits on empty rows. It exports directly to HubSpot, Salesforce, Instantly, and CSV, and supports TypeScript columns for custom scoring logic if you want it.


Where Orange Slice is not the right choice: if your workflow depends on calling obscure third-party APIs inside individual cells — the kind of deeply custom logic some Clay power users build — Clay's raw flexibility is still greater. Orange Slice is built for teams who want the output without the configuration overhead.


SDR teams and founders doing their own outbound tend to get the most from it. See[how it handles the full prospecting workflow](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/lead-generation-agent) if list-building is your primary need.


### Is Apollo.io a Good Clay Replacement?


Apollo is the most common Clay alternative for SDR teams, and for good reason. It bundles a large contact database with enrichment, sequencing, and basic analytics in one platform. Onboarding is fast, pricing is predictable per seat, and most SDRs can use it without RevOps support.


The trade-offs are real. Apollo uses a single data source model — if Apollo's database doesn't have a record, you get a blank with no fallback. Data freshness on niche personas (early-stage startups, specific international markets, non-English job titles) degrades noticeably. And the sequencing features, while convenient, aren't as sophisticated as dedicated tools like Instantly or Outreach.


Apollo is a strong choice when your ICP is well-covered by a large US-centric database and you want everything in one tab. Apollo publishes its own data methodology on[apollo.io](https://www.apollo.io/data-privacy) .


### When Does Clearbit (HubSpot Enrichment) Make Sense?


Clearbit was acquired by HubSpot and is now available as a native enrichment layer inside HubSpot. If your team lives in HubSpot and wants firmographic and technographic data appended to records automatically, this is the lowest-friction option available. No CSV exports, no field mapping, no sync jobs.


The limitation is that it only works inside HubSpot. It's not a prospecting tool — it enriches records that already exist in your CRM. If you need to build net-new lists, you still need a separate source. HubSpot's official product page for Breeze Intelligence (formerly Clearbit) describes the feature set at[hubspot.com](https://www.hubspot.com/products/marketing/breeze-intelligence) .


### What Does Lusha Do Well?


Lusha is a contact data provider focused on email and phone lookup. It has a browser extension that surfaces contact details on LinkedIn profiles, a small prospecting database, and CRM integrations. It's fast and simple for individual SDRs who need a quick lookup workflow.


It doesn't do waterfall enrichment, doesn't cover firmographics or technographics deeply, and isn't built for bulk list enrichment at scale. Think of it as a point solution for contact data rather than a full enrichment platform. Lusha's coverage and compliance approach is documented at[lusha.com](https://www.lusha.com/data-compliance/) .


### Where Does Phantombuster Fit?


Phantombuster is a LinkedIn scraping tool that automates actions — profile visits, connection requests, data extraction — at scale. It's useful for building raw lists from LinkedIn without Sales Navigator and for automating LinkedIn outreach sequences.


It requires more technical comfort than the other tools here, it operates in a gray area with LinkedIn's terms of service, and it produces raw data that still needs enrichment before it's usable. Phantombuster pairs well with an enrichment layer on top; it's not a standalone solution. The tool's automation library is listed at[phantombuster.com](https://phantombuster.com/automations) .

## How to Choose the Right Clay Alternative for Your Team


### If you're an SDR team without a dedicated RevOps person


You need a tool that doesn't require formula logic to operate. Apollo or Orange Slice both fit. Apollo if your ICP maps well to a large database; Orange Slice if you need richer signal data (funding rounds, tech stack, hiring signals) and want waterfall enrichment without building it yourself.


Check the[use cases page](https://www.orangeslice.ai/use-cases) for specific outbound plays that map to each workflow.


### If you're a founder doing your own outbound


You want speed and signal quality over raw volume. A chat-first interface where you describe your ICP and get a verified list back in minutes is more useful than a spreadsheet with 40 provider columns to configure. Orange Slice was built with this workflow in mind. The[lead generation agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/lead-generation-agent) handles the prospecting side; the[data enrichment agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/data-enrichment-agent) handles verification and signal appending.


### If you're a RevOps team managing CRM hygiene at scale


You need waterfall enrichment, clean CRM sync, and the ability to re-enrich records on a schedule. Clay is genuinely strong here if you have the technical resources to configure it. If you don't, Orange Slice's[CRM agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/crm-agent) handles enrichment, deduplication, and sync without requiring custom API work.


### If you're budget-constrained


Run a sample test before committing to any platform. Take 200 records from your actual ICP and run them through each tool's free tier or trial. Compare fill rates on the fields that matter to you — email, phone, job title, company size. The tool with the best fill rate on your specific ICP is worth more than the one with the longest feature list.


See[pricing](https://www.orangeslice.ai/pricing) for how Orange Slice's credit model compares to per-seat alternatives.

## What Does Waterfall Enrichment Actually Mean in Practice?


This term comes up in every enrichment conversation, so it's worth being precise.


**Single-source enrichment:** you send a record to one provider. If they have the email, you get it. If they don't, the field stays blank.


**Waterfall enrichment:** you send the record to provider A. If A returns nothing, it automatically goes to provider B. If B returns nothing, it goes to provider C. You pay only for successful hits (in most models), and your fill rate is dramatically higher.


For SDR teams building outbound lists, fill rate is everything. A list where 40% of emails are missing is a list where 40% of your sequences never send. Waterfall enrichment is not a nice-to-have — it's the difference between a usable list and a broken campaign.


Clay and Orange Slice both support waterfall enrichment natively. Apollo, Lusha, and Clearbit do not.


---


## One Real Workflow to Illustrate the Difference


Here's what a typical enrichment workflow looks like on a Clay alternative versus Clay itself.


**On Clay:** Import a CSV, add provider columns one by one (Hunter for email, Clearbit for firmographics, PeopleDataLabs as fallback), write a formula to cascade through them, map the output columns, set up a Zapier zap to push to HubSpot. Total setup: 2–4 hours for someone who knows what they're doing.


**On Orange Slice:** Describe the ICP in the chat. The[workflow](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/workflows) auto-populates enrichment columns, runs waterfall across providers, verifies emails, and exports to HubSpot with field mapping. Total setup: under 20 minutes.


The Clay workflow is more customizable. The Orange Slice workflow is faster to run and maintain. Which matters more depends on how complex your enrichment logic actually needs to be.


---


## Where Does Clay Still Win?


If you have a technical RevOps operator who wants to build enrichment logic that calls custom APIs, chains AI prompts inside cells, or integrates with tools that don't have native connectors — Clay is still the most flexible option available. It's a platform for builders.


According to[Clay's own documentation](https://clay.com/) , the platform connects to over 100 data providers and supports custom HTTP API calls directly inside table cells — a level of raw extensibility none of the alternatives here match. If that's your requirement, Clay is the honest answer.


If you want enrichment to be a workflow your SDRs run themselves without a ticket to RevOps, the alternatives above are better fits. Start with the tool that matches your team's actual technical capacity, not the one with the most features on the comparison page.


The[lead qualification agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/lead-qualification-agent) is a useful next step if you want to score and route enriched leads automatically once your list is built.
